Select sensoraia_dipla_cam_cyberzoo_demo.xml instead of the original sensoraia_dipla_cam_demo.xml. It retains the same START, load-eight, follow-eight, STOP, return and landing sequence, with the supplied Cyberzoo corners and a centre at local east/north (0,0). It commands 1 m height, limits survey speed to 0.35 m/s, and requires 20 cm horizontal arrival at each P1..P8. These explicit arrival checks do not inherit an airframe's larger outdoor waypoint radius. Survey entry requires a 15 cm centre check and height between 0.9 and 1.1 m before the first anchor is captured.

Use the supplied worker profile modules/dipla_cam/diplacam-cyberzoo.ini:

field=modules/dipla_cam/data/map_26_NAIP_grid_counts.csv
cadence_ms=100
planning_pose_max_age_ms=3000
field_size_m=4
field_rotation_deg=125
flight_height_m=1
flight_height_tolerance_m=0.15

field_size_m is the physical side of the square, from 1 to 100 m; its default is 100. field_rotation_deg rotates the model's X axis counterclockwise from east, from -180 to 180 degrees; its default is zero. The 125-degree orientation follows the supplied room edges. The complete 4 m square has at least 0.58 m nominal clearance inside the supplied inner polygon before anchor or tracking error. The model's existing two-cell margin adds a further 0.16 m inset along each square edge.

All three measured coordinates use the same scale: physical metres are multiplied by 100 / field_size_m before planning. Thus 4 m maps to the unchanged 100-unit field, and a real 1 m AGL maps to 25 model units. Position, sensor footprint, CSV field and GP length scales remain geometrically consistent; stretching X and Y independently or rescaling only output points would not preserve them. Predicted model Z is still discarded. Returned XY points are rotated and scaled back into physical metres, while the aircraft continues to command 1 m. Field-value noise variance is not a distance and is not rescaled. The graph, normalization constants and twenty DDIM steps are unchanged; no retraining is implied.

flight_height_m defaults to 2 m and accepts 0.2..40 m. flight_height_tolerance_m defaults to 0.75 m and must be positive and less than the selected height. A resized survey is rejected unless its entire accepted height interval maps inside the model's 10..40 altitude domain. The profile above maps 0.85..1.15 physical metres to 21.25..28.75 model units. Its 3000 ms planning-pose admission setting accommodates the initial MORA GP update while the aircraft holds CENTRE. The existing point freshness and flight-plan loading limits remain unchanged. Reading retained route points is independent of processing a pending sensor observation, so expensive GP work does not serialize delivery of P1..P8. Point-only reads do not create additional sensor observations; every admitted observation is processed once. Resized profiles use the diffusion planner; the optional fixed-height CMA-ES comparison rejects them explicitly. The original outdoor profile retains its original fixed 2 m synthetic footprint, while resized profiles use the measured, uniformly scaled AGL for both their sensor footprint and neural conditioning.

For a PC-only native session, build make usher diplacam from the Sensoraia root. The launcher selects diplacam-cyberzoo.ini automatically when the saved aircraft configuration selects the Cyberzoo plan. The original plan selects diplacam-nps.ini. No worker-profile environment setting is needed.

Start Center from the Paparazzi directory. The explicit empty UART override below keeps this test entirely on the PC even with a MORA cable connected. Clear an old experiment override so automatic profile selection can work:

unset DIPLACAM_CONFIG
cd "$HOME/paparazzi"
MORA_UART_DEVICE="" ./paparazzi

docs.title: Manual Cyberzoo NPS Flight
docs.text:
1. Stop the old session programs. In Center select Bebop_DIPLACAM (airframes/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_parrot_bebop.xml) and choose flight_plans/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_dipla_cam_cyberzoo_demo.xml as the flight plan. Save the configuration and confirm the Flight Plan field contains cyberzoo before building. If the XML was edited outside Center, reload the configuration first so a cached selection cannot overwrite that edit.
  2. Select target nps, build it, then use session Sensoraia Diplacam NPS in userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_control_panel.xml. Do not select either MORA session for this PC-only test. If Center was open while its panel changed, switch to another control panel and back to Sensoraia to reload the program arguments.
  3. Start the session's five programs: Sensoraia USHER, Sensoraia NPS, Data Link, Server, and GCS Classic. The USHER console must print worker profile: followed by diplacam-cyberzoo.ini. The simulator console must report PC execution. An already running USHER does not reload its profile when the flight plan changes; restart that program as well as NPS.
  4. In the GCS select mode Nav. Wait for a valid position and Ground standby after Wait GPS and Geo init. NPS supplies this position; physical OptiTrack hardware is not needed for this simulation.
  5. Press Takeoff. This starts the motors and climbs while holding the takeoff position. Wait for Standby at approximately 1 m. Do not manually start Start Dipla, Load eight, or Follow.
  6. Press Dipla once. The aircraft moves to CENTRE, settles within 15 cm at 0.9..1.1 m, then passes through Start Dipla and Load eight. Once all eight points are accepted it enters Follow eight automatically. These short transition blocks can be missed in telemetry.
  7. Check that P1..P8 lie in the small rotated survey square and that the aircraft follows them at 1 m. A route is retained while its eight points are followed; a new batch is requested after that route completes. USHER prints one anchor_lat_e7 for the survey and successive diplacam chunk= records. No JPEG files or yellow DC_SHOT markers are expected: this is a file-backed sensor experiment, and its shot-report mask is 239.
  8. Press Return, wait until the aircraft is back at HOME, then press Land Here. Completion is Ground standby with the motors off, not merely entry into a landing block.

If the aircraft takes off to 2 m, the outdoor plan was built. If the USHER console names diplacam-nps.ini while the aircraft holds 1 m, the peer and flight plan do not match. Stop both, save the Cyberzoo selection, clear any DIPLACAM_CONFIG override, and restart the session. If Load eight returns to Standby, inspect the USHER console for worker/configuration errors; pressing Follow does not bypass the missing-route checks.

On MORA, select the indoor worker profile through USHER's --diplacam-config argument instead of the outdoor profile. Automatic PC-launcher selection does not reconfigure an already running service on MORA. The normal deployment can package this profile directly:

make mora-deploy MORA_PROFILE=diplacam \
   DIPLA_WORKER_CONFIG="$PWD/modules/dipla_cam/diplacam-cyberzoo.ini"

The package keeps the selected geometry and timing settings, replaces field with share/diplacam/field.csv, and includes the selected field data. Omit DIPLA_WORKER_CONFIG to package the original outdoor profile. Model and conditioning-cache selection remain separate application settings.

For physical Cyberzoo use, the aircraft's OptiTrack input must feed its normal position/INS and GPS-validity interface with the same geographic origin and east/north orientation as the supplied plan. Paparazzi's gps_datalink publishes valid external tracking as a 3D fix, so the existing GpsFixValid() gates remain meaningful without an indoor GNSS receiver. The supplied Bebop airframe still selects Furuno GPS; selecting the plan does not reconfigure that aircraft input. Clocking, tracking alignment and room coordinates must be checked on the actual installation. The existing geographic UART points have 1e-7-degree quantization, about 11 mm north and 7 mm east here.

Local NPS exercises the native USHER/Diplacam path, room geometry, point sequencing, return and landing. It does not measure OptiTrack or physical flight accuracy. The supplied field remains a scaled file-backed experiment, not an added physical sensor driver.

docs.title: Run The PC Demo
docs.text:
With Paparazzi installed at ~/paparazzi, build native USHER and Diplacam and link the demo configurations from the Sensoraia root:

make usher diplacam
./kickstart.sh

./kickstart.sh installs sensoraia_demo_conf.xml, the unified control panel sensoraia_demo_control_panel.xml, and symlinks for the Sensoraia flight plans and Bebop_DIPLACAM rotorcraft airframe into ~/paparazzi/conf/ (preserving previous conf.xml and control_panel.xml links under ~/.local/state/sensoraia/kickstart/). No Python simulation adapter is used.

  1. Start Paparazzi Center (cd ~/paparazzi && ./paparazzi), select Bebop_DIPLACAM and target nps, then click Build.
  2. Select control panel userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_control_panel.xml and session Sensoraia Diplacam NPS, then click Execute.
  3. In GCS wait for valid telemetry and Ground standby. Select NAV mode before pressing Takeoff.
  4. When the aircraft settles at 2 m in Standby, press Dipla (the Begin survey block). It approaches CENTRE, dwells there, seeds the initial P8 hold at the current position, and enters Start Dipla.
  5. The first admitted shot anchors the field. The mission fills P1..P8 from native cam-point replies and enters Follow eight automatically. P1..P8 stay fixed while that route is flown. On completing the path, the mission requests and loads the next route.
  6. Press Return, wait until the aircraft is back at HOME, then press Land Here. Wait for Ground standby and motors off before stopping the session programs.

With no cable, the session starts exactly one local USHER, which starts its native Diplacam worker on demand. With a cable, the same session skips the PC peer and uses MORA. The NPS console prints execution: PC or execution: MORA, followed by the selected UART device. The launcher refreshes the selected NPS transport build before starting, including when the cable choice changed since Center's Build action. There is no separate waypoint adapter. The simulator runs at real time because freshness checks use elapsed wall-clock time. The flight plan holds at the configured HOLD point if initial loading times out or updates stop.

docs.title: Deploy Diplacam To MORA
docs.text:
Prepare the board once using Install and get started. The ready-made release targets 64-bit Trixie on the Pi Zero 2 W reference board. The examples below use air@theatre.local and /home/air/sensoraia.

From the Sensoraia root on your PC:

make -j32 mora-deploy MORA_PROFILE=diplacam MORA_SSH_TARGET=air@theatre.local

This builds the ARM64 applications on the PC, packages Diplacam with its matching ONNX Runtime, model, settings and field CSV, uploads the release, and starts USHER on MORA. Repeat the same command for an update. No compiler or Python planner is installed on the board. To prepare the release without contacting MORA, use make -j32 mora-package MORA_PROFILE=diplacam instead.

Every Diplacam package includes the complete modules/dipla_cam/models/ directory, including additional models, metadata and data files, under share/diplacam/models/ on MORA. Redeployment refreshes these files even when they are not the selected model. Copying another model does not select it or establish that it is compatible with the current planner; the application settings still choose the active graph, descriptor and metadata. The default full-suite make mora-deploy includes Diplacam and these assets automatically while starting Spottercam by default; MORA_PROFILE=diplacam starts USHER with the packaged Diplacam worker configuration. The dedicated MORA_PROFILE=lwircam remains an LWIR-only package and service.

The diplacam profile packages USHER, Diplacam and their runtime assets, without the unrelated camera applications or their OS dependencies. It does not start LWIRcam or EARcam. USHER uses the board UART, normally /dev/serial0, and starts its native Diplacam worker when the mission requests it. This remains the supplied CSV-field experiment, not a physical spectrum-camera driver. Deploying does not arm an aircraft or start an NPS session.

The installed worker configuration is /home/air/sensoraia/share/diplacam/example.ini; it selects the packaged share/diplacam/field.csv. Model and experiment settings are beside it in share/diplacam/diplacam_settings.ini. The service working directory is the installation root. The PC demo instead uses modules/dipla_cam/diplacam-nps.ini; its paths point into the source checkout.

Confirm the selected service:

ssh air@theatre.local 'systemctl --no-pager --full status usher.service'
ssh air@theatre.local 'journalctl -u usher.service -n 50 --no-pager'

Expect an active USHER service whose command includes --diplacam-config. If activation needs administrative authentication, follow Deployment recovery using the staging path printed by that upload. A running service confirms startup; returned planner points are checked in the next exercise.

docs.title: Simulate With Diplacam On MORA
docs.text:
Keep the aircraft simulated on the PC while the real board runs USHER and Diplacam. Connect the laptop FTDI adapter to MORA using the desk-test wiring: 5 V power, common ground and crossed 3.3 V UART. Leave a real flight controller disconnected for this exercise. Wi-Fi/SSH carries deployment and logs; the FTDI UART carries flight requests and returned points at 115200 baud.

  1. Deploy the Diplacam profile above and stop the previous Sensoraia session.
  2. Connect the MORA FTDI cable.
  3. Ensure ./kickstart.sh has been run once from the Sensoraia root, then start Paparazzi Center from ~/paparazzi:
./kickstart.sh
cd ~/paparazzi && ./paparazzi

Select Bebop_DIPLACAM, target nps, userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_control_panel.xml, and the ordinary Sensoraia Diplacam NPS session. The cable is selected automatically; the PC peer entry prints that it is using MORA instead of starting local USHER. Sensoraia MORA desk NPS is also available when you want startup to require a cable rather than permit PC-only operation. With an already open Center, stop the old session and reload the control panel after running ./kickstart.sh.

Detection uses a single FTDI by-id device, otherwise /dev/ttyUSB0. If you have several FTDI adapters, choose MORA's actual path explicitly when starting Center:

cd ~/paparazzi && MORA_UART_DEVICE=/dev/serial/by-id/usb-FTDI_YOUR_ADAPTER ./paparazzi

Both NPS serial endpoints are pinned to that device in a hardware session, so a local peer cannot take over later. A leftover /tmp/usher-sim makes startup stop with an explanation instead of silently testing the PC. End the earlier local session before retrying. No serial monitor should own the same FTDI port.

Use the same NAV, Takeoff, Dipla, Return and Land Here sequence as Run the PC demo. Run NPS at real time. Watch the board in another PC terminal:

ssh -t air@theatre.local 'journalctl -fu usher.service'

After Dipla reaches Start Dipla, inspect the native processes:

ssh air@theatre.local 'ps -o pid,ppid,pcpu,rss,etime,args -C usher -C diplacam'

During the survey, diplacam is a child of the board's usher; its PPID matches USHER's PID. The journal reports anchor_lat_e7, initial_gp_update_ms, and successive chunk=... inference_ms=... lines. Before Dipla, and after a STOP/Return ends the survey, only USHER may be present. Its --diplacam-config argument enables the backend; it does not keep a planner busy continuously. Low idle CPU is normal, and CPU alone cannot identify where a route was computed.

Check all of these before calling the exercise successful:

  • The MORA journal shows Diplacam starting, the first-position anchor, and planner results while the simulated aircraft requests measurements.
  • GCS receives all eight P1–P8 updates and the mission enters Follow eight.
  • The simulated aircraft follows the retained route at 2 m, then requests another chunk without moving the geographic anchor.
  • Return reaches HOME and Land Here ends in Ground standby with motors off.

Diplacam does not produce JPEGs in this experiment, and its normal mission suppresses Diplacam-only shot markers. Inspect returned points and the board journal, not photo counts. UART errors, worker failures or an expired loading deadline are failed results, even if USHER remains active. PC simulation results alone do not establish the board's planning latency or memory headroom.

Stop the Center session after landing; the managed USHER service stays on MORA. To return to PC-only simulation, disconnect the cable and restart the session. To deliberately keep the cable attached while using the PC, start Center with MORA_UART_DEVICE="" ./paparazzi; the explicitly empty value disables cable selection for that session.

docs.title: If The Demo Stops
docs.text:
Symptom Action ./kickstart.sh reports missing Paparazzi Install Paparazzi (or set PAPARAZZI_HOME), then repeat ./kickstart.sh Native binaries not built yet Run make usher diplacam from the Sensoraia root Center shows an old aircraft or session Select userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_conf.xml and userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_control_panel.xml NPS reports no compiled aircraft Select Bebop_DIPLACAM, target nps, and build before starting the session No local UART connection Check the printed execution location first; a cable-selected session uses board USHER, not a local peer Entry remains at CENTRE Check GPS, height and arrival/dwell conditions; the mission has not started measurements yet Loading returns to Standby Inspect the USHER console for model, field or pose errors; The USHER console contains native worker diagnostics and shot results. The worker reports the captured anchor latitude/longitude in integer 1e-7-degree units and the shot number that established it. Kickoff keeps the build log and standalone preflight output under ~/.local/state/sensoraia/kickoff/ (or the corresponding XDG_STATE_HOME).

docs.title: Understand A Refresh
docs.text:
The flight plan owns route completion, including Paparazzi's configured arrival margin and segment-passing rules. Diplacam does not run a second arrival check. Its eight XY targets stay fixed until the path completes. The mission then requests the next chunk using the existing START command, holds at P8 while loading, and enters Follow only after all eight slots have arrived. Active START retains both the geographic anchor and accumulated belief; STOP ends that survey. The repeating chunk loop does not revisit CENTRE.

Initial loading uses P8 seeded at the entry position. Later loading holds at the previous route's P8. Worker loss cannot silently relocate the survey: USHER rejects further chunk starts until STOP explicitly ends the lost survey.

USHER retrieves pinned slots and the FC applies them through its existing camera-point API, preserving the configured 2 m height. The eight moves are not atomic, so the mission loads them before following the new chunk. HOME and landing points never move. The GCS displays points; it does not plan the route.

The worker has one GP owner and room for 64 pending observations. If processing cannot keep up and that queue fills, it invalidates the route and reports the failure instead of silently losing measurements. The mission's existing timeout then returns it to Standby. Resolve the cause and restart the session programs before trying again. A retained route also requires continuing fresh observation replies; a long execution is not permission to replay stale replies.

Entering Standby, Return or landing clears loaded-route readiness. Press Dipla to load a fresh route before following again; manually selecting Follow eight does not reuse a stopped route.

docs.title: Control GCS Shot Markers
docs.text:
The supplied mission suppresses DC_SHOT telemetry for Diplacam-only triggers, so repeated measurements do not add yellow shot circles to the GCS. P1..P8 updates, capture requests, shot numbering and returned results continue normally. This does not clear circles already drawn; use Clear DCSHOTS for those.

The UART module's shot report mask setting is independent of its camera mask, which selects what to trigger:

Report Mask Behavior 255 (0xff) Report triggers from every camera slot 239 (0xef) Silence Diplacam-only triggers; keep other cameras' reports 0 Silence all shot reports without disabling captures

A mixed trigger still produces one report if any requested camera's bit is enabled. A silent trigger still advances its shot number once, after UART admission. Rejected requests advance neither numbering nor reports. Silent shots are absent from DC_SHOT telemetry logs, not from the camera protocol.

For an aircraft startup default, add this define to its existing UART module:

<module name="digital_cam_uart">
   <define name="DIGITAL_CAM_UART_SHOT_REPORT_MASK" value="239"/>
</module>

Omitting the define preserves normal reporting (255). A flight plan can set the policy before starting autoshoot:

<call_once fun="uart_cam_ctrl_set_shot_report_mask(239)"/>

The supplied Start Dipla block applies 239 each time it starts. To keep reports enabled in this mission, change that call to 255. During a session, change control / tb / shot report mask in the GCS settings to toggle reports without rebuilding or restarting USHER. Include modules/digital_cam_uart.xml in the aircraft's settings_modules list to expose that setting; the supplied configuration already does so. Only integer masks 0..255 are accepted.

Runtime changes override the startup default and survive a USHER reconnect; entering Start Dipla reapplies the mission's value. No GCS or USHER update is needed for this policy, but the FC must be rebuilt with the matching UART module and generated settings.

docs.title: Compare With CMA-ES
docs.text:
cmaes=true in the settings explicitly selects the classical comparison planner instead of ONNX diffusion. It is not a fallback after model failure. Use the same field/observations when comparing results; one attractive route does not establish a model's performance.

Setting Default Meaning And Accepted Values cmaes_budget_ms 1000 Cooperative whole-search budget, integer 1..4000 ms cmaes_maxfevals 300 Objective evaluation ceiling, integer 12..3000; population size remains 12 cmaes_seed 55 Positive optimizer seed, integer 1..2147483647 cmaes_utility_threshold 0.3 Finite importance threshold in field units cmaes_confidence_beta 1 Finite nonnegative multiplier of posterior standard deviation cmaes_step_xy_m 20 Positive finite initial XY search standard deviation, in metres

These settings are validated at startup even when cmaes=false, but affect only the selected comparison planner. It uses the same GP/sensor profile and flight margin as diffusion. Cancelled or incomplete searches publish no partial route. A tight wall-clock budget can interrupt a search at different points under different load; a fixed seed does not make timed-out runs identical.

docs.title: ONNX Runtime
docs.text:
Diplacam uses the shared native runtime, with one default inference thread and a budget for the whole plan. See model selection for compatible assignments and packaging.

onnx_threads accepts 1..32. The supplied INI sets inference_timeout_ms=4000 for all twenty passes together; omitting that key uses the shared application default of 2000 ms. These are cooperative limits, not hard-real-time guarantees.

docs.title: Before Onboard Use
docs.text:
The simulation exercises native USHER/Diplacam IPC and the shared FC point transport. It does not establish real-sensor performance, MORA resource headroom or field accuracy. The configured NPS height is supplied from the simulated FC state; a physical installation needs its own valid height source.

Check real sensor integration, model usefulness at the intended height, terrain/clearance, aircraft response and combined board resource use before relying on an onboard mission. The dense field belief alone uses substantial memory; one process's average size is not whole-board headroom.

docs.title: EARcam: Search By Sound
docs.text:
EARcam listens for an alarm through a USB microphone and combines sound measurements with aircraft positions to estimate a useful search location. Start by listening on the bench, then try the supplied simulated flight.

Sound-search terms | Simulated flights

docs.title: Listen On The Bench
docs.text:
From the Sensoraia root:

make -j32 earcam
arecord -L
bin/earcam --device hw:CARD=Device,DEV=0

Use the actual ALSA device listed on your computer, not necessarily the example name. Stop with Ctrl+C. Place the intended alarm in a controlled test area and confirm its tone is detected before adding aircraft noise.

Keep microphone gain and mounting fixed during a comparison. A dramatic volume knob is useful for music and much less useful for measuring whether you moved closer to a sound source.

docs.title: What The Readings Mean
docs.text:
EARcam looks for useful tone energy rather than treating every loud sound as the desired alarm. Its signal checks reduce the influence of unrelated noise, but wind, propulsion, reflections and alarm direction still matter.

Digital microphone levels are normally dBFS, not calibrated dB SPL. Relative changes can be useful with fixed gain; physical sound-pressure and rough distance estimates need the appropriate microphone calibration.

Observation Interpretation Stronger clean alarm tone Useful evidence, not a location by itself Loud broadband noise May be wind/propulsion rather than the target Clipped samples Reduce excessive gain and repeat the check No accepted tone Check device, frequency band, gain and the actual alarm

docs.title: How It Finds The Source
docs.text:
One microphone does not point at the alarm. Movement supplies different measurement positions; the software fits a sound model to useful readings and reduces the effect of outliers. It does not simply select the single loudest sample's coordinates.

At height, small horizontal movements near the source can change loudness very little. Several useful passes around an area provide better geometry than assuming the peak of one pass is an exact fix. Wind and reflections can also distort the apparent peak.

The result is a search aid. Independent measurements are needed before claiming position accuracy or making a rescue or flight-safety decision.

docs.title: Try A Simulated Search
docs.text:
Use the Paparazzi demo setup. The EARcam session runs USHER natively with a simulated alarm source, so no physical microphone or MORA board is needed:

make -j32 usher soda earcam
./kickstart.sh

Start Paparazzi Center (cd ~/paparazzi && ./paparazzi), select userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_conf.xml, aircraft Easystar_3_EARCAM (or your own fixed-wing aircraft assigned flight_plans/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_ear_cam_demo.xml), and target nps, then click Build. In the Session tab select userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_control_panel.xml and start Sensoraia EARcam NPS. Wait for live telemetry/GPS in GCS Classic, then click Takeoff; the plan climbs and enters its flower listening mission automatically.

Watch the search pattern, result stage and normal landing. An accepted answer can update TARGET; a timeout or unusable answer can finish without a fix. A completed simulated search does not establish microphone performance.

docs.title: Use With USHER
docs.text:
Choose the microphone device and a suitable alarm band in the actual USHER configuration. A separately managed live listening session can use:

./usher --earcam --earcam-band 2400,3200 --debug

The band is an example for the intended alarm, not a universal setting for every sound. Avoid another program owning the same input. Check the sensor alone before combining it with other workloads on MORA.

Capture uses nonblocking PCM reads with waits of at most 100 ms. Two seconds without PCM progress, including persistent device suspension, fails the worker so USHER can supervise its restart. This is a device-progress check, not a sound-level gate: quiet audio still contains PCM samples.

USHER rejects timed measurements whose original audio-window end is more than 500 ms old; a late classifier completion cannot make old audio fresh again. Unknown chunk timing leaves the whole classifier window explicitly unaligned. These are software policies, not measured USB latency or synchronization accuracy.

docs.title: Inspect The Search Result
docs.text: Keep the recorded observations, position context and generated sound picture. The JPEG is a computed heat map, not a photograph taken by a microphone. Inspect result validity before treating it as a current target.

docs.title: Replay And View A Heatmap On A Map
docs.text:
The replay and overlay applications run on the development PC. Replay rebuilds the EARcam heatmap from a saved session log; overlay adds satellite context and redraws the source marker and optional observation/flight tracks. This is a visual review tool, not another localization step, and it never changes the recorded measurements.

Build both native programs from the Sensoraia root, then replay the session log to create the decorated image, its .geo sidecar and an undecorated _field.jpg:

make -j32 ear_heatmap_replay ear_heatmap_overlay
bin/ear_heatmap_replay /path/to/ear-session.csv /path/to/ear-result.jpg

Overlay that result, optionally adding the session samples, aircraft track, search center and a known simulation source:

bin/ear_heatmap_overlay /path/to/ear-result.jpg \
  --log /path/to/ear-session.csv \
  --track /path/to/aircraft-track.csv \
  --search 48.8105,7.8516,25 \
  --truth 48.8105,7.8516

The default output is ear-result_sat.jpg. The application automatically uses the matching _field.jpg and .geo files when present; keep all three replay outputs together. --search takes latitude, longitude and optional radius in metres. Use --truth only when the known position is available, such as in a simulation; it is drawn separately from the estimated loudest spot.

Google imagery reuses Paparazzi GCS's existing ~/.local/share/paparazzi/pprzgcs/map/GOOGLE/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpeg cache by default (or $XDG_DATA_HOME/paparazzi/pprzgcs/map when XDG_DATA_HOME is set). --source esri selects Esri imagery, and --cache DIR chooses the cache root. Existing tiles are opened directly; there is no network-library dependency. On a cache miss, the program uses the system curl command to fetch that tile. Add --offline to require a complete local cache and fail instead of attempting a download. Tile imagery is visual context only: it cannot improve acoustic evidence or turn an uncertain estimate into ground truth.

Use bin/ear_heatmap_overlay --help for zoom, opacity, margin, obstacle-grid, and other options. An obstacle CSV, when available, must contain x_east_m,lat,lon,mnh_m columns.

docs.title: Optional ONNX Sound Classification
docs.text: Select a compatible assignment in earcam_settings.ini. The model must match the declared PCM sample rate and window; its probability is separate from raw microphone level. A classifier does not automatically provide a geographic source. See model selection.

docs.title: Why Height And More Than One Pass Matter
docs.text:
In an ideal free field, doubling source distance reduces sound pressure by about 6 dB. On an aircraft, slant distance includes height: at 40 m above a source, moving 10 m sideways changes the distance only to about 41.2 m. That is roughly 0.26 dB, easily obscured by ordinary noise.

This broad, nearly flat loudness peak is why the loudest single reading is not an exact ground location. Passes from different directions help constrain the fit. Reflections, alarm orientation and propulsion can distort the pattern; the distance relationship explains the method, not a guaranteed useful range for every installation.

docs.title: Read Level, Tone And Quality Together
docs.text:
Where the selected mode reports these diagnostics:

Reading What It Tells You Level Strength of the selected tone, not all nearby sound Frequency Which tone is strongest within the selected search band Contrast How distinct that tone is from the remaining in-band sound Envelope/trend Smoothed change across pulses: approaching, receding or steady Alarm/clip flags Whether tone checks passed or the recording range was exceeded

Compare a clean alarm recording with quiet/background and propulsion/noise conditions. Strong RMS alone does not identify the alarm. Keep microphone, gain and mounting fixed when comparing positions or runs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Check the correct audio device, gain, clipping and whether the alarm is actually within the selected band. Compare quiet and propulsion/noise conditions. If readings change after moving the microphone or changing gain, start a new controlled comparison rather than combining incompatible measurements into one search.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Sound and shared project definitions live in the Sensoraia glossary, including its dedicated EARcam section.

docs.title: Read The Information In Your Photos
docs.text:
A photo is more useful when you know where it came from. Sensoraia keeps available aircraft, capture and analysis information with supported JPEGs using EXIF metadata. Keep the original images: editing or exporting them through another program may discard that information.

Metadata terms | Capture with USHER

docs.title: Inspect A Saved JPEG
docs.text:
On the PC, ExifTool can display the supported records without changing them:

sudo apt install libimage-exiftool-perl
exiftool -G1 -a -s /absolute/path/photo.jpg

Start with the image dimensions, GPS fields, image description and user comment. Read the whole record rather than assuming a single GPS field says everything about a capture. A generic viewer may not display custom evidence.

Information What It Helps You Check Camera and photo identity Which observation a result belongs to Position, altitude and attitude Where the aircraft was reported and how it was oriented Request/observation timing Whether the pose describes a request or an estimated sensing interval Mock or lens-emulation records Whether the pixels are simulated or derived Detection or thermal records What optional processing returned

Availability depends on the backend. Missing data must not be interpreted as zero, and a precise-looking coordinate is not a measured accuracy claim.

docs.title: Request Pose Is Not Always Exposure Pose
docs.text:
The aircraft can move between requesting a capture and the actual exposure. Where supported timing evidence is available, Sensoraia can estimate a pose for the observation interval. Other captures retain the request-time pose.

When comparing a detected object with a ground reference, check which timing information is actually present. At 10 m/s, a tenth of a second corresponds to about one metre of travel, before other errors are considered.

docs.title: Embedded Capture And LOOM Evidence
docs.text:
Native camera paths can retain capture identity and timing inside the JPEG. LOOMcam can also retain model-related features. These records help associate processing with the correct frame; they do not prove physical timing accuracy or make an unspecified feature vector a navigation direction.

Stock camera tools do not necessarily provide the same evidence. A usable photo can therefore have less qualified timing than another backend's photo. Do not copy evidence records from a different image to make it appear complete.

docs.title: Original, Review Copy And Sidecar
docs.text:
The original flight JPEG is the archive. SODA may create separate annotated copies or crops, and saved-image model analysis may write a neighbouring result file. Keep required sidecars with their source image.

Thermal JPEGs may also contain a temperature plane. A resized screenshot or colourized export cannot replace those samples. Use the LWIRcam guide for supported readback.

docs.title: Use Photos For Mapping Or Evaluation
docs.text:
Use original images and the input contract required by PANGEA. An arbitrary GPS-tagged JPEG may lack the attitude, height or camera geometry needed by a mapping workflow.

For model evaluation, retain the image's origin, model identity and independent labels. Provider imagery terms still apply to MIMIC-derived material.

docs.title: If A Field Looks Wrong
docs.text: Check the sensor, coordinate units, altitude reference and timing first. Compare an original with any edited copy to see whether metadata was removed. If the backend never supplied a measurement, changing an EXIF field cannot recover it. Keep the original and investigate the capture source instead.

docs.title: Read A Detailed Application Record
docs.text:
Inspect the text payload without the rest of ExifTool's listing:

exiftool -b -UserComment /absolute/path/photo.jpg

Look for sensor/result type, photo identity, available pose/time information and whether observations are simulated. Field availability varies by backend; an absent measurement is different from a valid zero.

If an object position looks wrong, first distinguish the aircraft's GPS tag from a projected target record. Then check timing, lens/mounting geometry and altitude reference. The coordinate alone does not explain those inputs.

docs.title: Install And Get Started
docs.text:
Welcome to Sensoraia. This guide takes you from a source checkout to a running camera service, first on your Linux PC and then on MORA. The Pi Zero 2 W is our initial reference board, not a requirement; you can stop after simulation or adapt the deployment to another compatible compute board.

The guide keeps PC preparation, local use and onboard deployment as separate steps, so you can take the route that matches the equipment you have today.

New to MORA, USHER or the abbreviations? Keep the Sensoraia glossary beside this guide. Its installation terms explain builds, packages, paths and deployment without assuming you already know the tools.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
For this task You need Build PC applications Linux, a C/C++ toolchain and the dependencies below Run a simulated flight A working Paparazzi NPS installation and the example aircraft configuration Deploy onboard A compatible Linux compute board; the current ready-made reference is Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W with 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Trixie Capture from hardware Your camera or USB microphone, correct cables and its runtime packages

The Pi is the deliberately modest starting point for resource planning, not the definition of MORA. Current ARM64 build and package instructions are for Raspberry Pi OS Trixie on that board. Other boards need matching binaries, runtime libraries, sensor drivers and interface configuration; verify their combined memory and processing capacity with the services you intend to run.

These examples use ~/develop/sensoraia, SSH user air, host theatre.local and install directory /home/air/sensoraia. Change them to match your machine. The packaged service currently runs as air; if you choose another account, review the service template before packaging.

Connect camera ribbon cables only with power off. For UART, use 3.3 V logic, crossed TX/RX and a common ground.

docs.title: 1. Prepare The Source Checkout
docs.text:
Clone the repository (make automatically syncs and checks out the pinned OpenCV 4.14.0 submodule into ext/opencv on first build, or pass --recurse-submodules to prefetch it during clone):

git clone https://github.com/OpenUAS/sensoraia.git ~/develop/sensoraia
cd ~/develop/sensoraia
make help

All product builds, self-contained Paparazzi demo airframes, flight plans, and simulation launchers are included directly in this repository. make help lists all supported build, camera-selection, packaging, and deployment commands.

docs.title: 2. Install PC Dependencies
docs.text:
On a Debian/Ubuntu development PC, start with:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install build-essential cmake meson ninja-build pkg-config \
  gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu g++-aarch64-linux-gnu \
  git curl ca-certificates gnupg openssl patch python3 python3-venv python3-jinja2 python3-yaml \
  libasound2-dev \
  rsync openssh-client

These are development-PC packages, installed once. The cross-compilers let the same PC build the ARM64 applications as well as native applications. No preinstalled libcamera-dev, private camera checkout or manual copying of camera headers is required: the normal build compiles its pinned native camera library from source into the checkout's private build area.

The first build needs Internet access to fetch checked source archives, build-tool Python packages and the Raspberry Pi OS Trixie SDK packages. Those downloads and SDK extraction do not require root access. Later builds reuse the prepared dependencies unless you clean them.

docs.title: 3. Build Native Applications
docs.text:
For the complete suite, run this from the checkout root:

make all

This is also the command to use after make clean. It prepares missing dependencies first, then compiles every Sensoraia application for both PC and ARM64. Parallel jobs are selected automatically; you do not need to remember -j or individual module targets.

The native camera library, YAML support and OpenCV are built from pinned or bundled sources. OpenCV 4.14.0 lives as a pinned Git submodule at ext/opencv in the checkout and is initialized automatically on first make. Every application's JPEG codec is built directly from OpenCV's bundled IJG sources; no system JPEG development package or separate JPEG download is required. OpenCV image-codec modules are not added. The ARM64 sysroot is prepared from signed Trixie packages, including camera and ALSA development files. All of this happens on the PC; no running MORA or SSH connection is needed to build.

Success looks like: a final list of every executable followed by:

Complete Sensoraia suite: 27 executables verified.

The build exits with an error if a required application is missing. A few completed compiler commands are not the completion report for the whole suite.

Built Application PC Output ARM64 Output USHER usher usher-arm64 SODA bin/soda bin/soda-arm64 Camera lens tool bin/camera_lens bin/camera_lens-arm64 PANGEA bin/pangea bin/pangea-arm64 LWIRcam bin/lwircam bin/lwircam-arm64 LWIR calibration bin/lwir_calibrate bin/lwir_calibrate-arm64 EARcam bin/earcam bin/earcam-arm64 Acoustic heatmap replay bin/ear_heatmap_replay bin/ear_heatmap_replay-arm64 LOOMcam bin/loomcam bin/loomcam-arm64 AIcam native photo worker bin/aicam bin/aicam-arm64 Spottercam bin/spottercam bin/spottercam-arm64 CHDKbridge bin/chdkbridge bin/chdkbridge-arm64 Diplacam bin/diplacam bin/diplacam-arm64 Acoustic heatmap overlay bin/ear_heatmap_overlay PC-only tool

AIcam and CHDK camera backends are integrated into USHER. The native AIcam photo worker and CHDKbridge can also be used separately. Building an application does not enable its sensor, install a model or start a service. Choose its guide below for the appropriate hardware, configuration and example workflow.

You should now have: usher at the project root and camera applications in bin/. Check without opening any hardware:

./usher --version
./bin/lwircam --version
./bin/pangea --version
make suite-check

Run make all again for normal updates; unchanged files and dependencies are reused. To cap parallel jobs, use make -j4 all; make -j1 all is serial. An intentional full cleanup is:

make clean
make all

make clean all is also ordered safely. Cleaning removes generated binaries, SDKs and build caches, so the next build downloads and prepares them again. It does not remove your installed PC prerequisite packages or source checkout. Use make -B all when you want to force rebuilding without deleting SDKs.

A build error is not a request to run make clean. The useful part is usually the first compiler or dependency error; the last line just reports that Make is disappointed too. See If Something Stops.

docs.title: Fly A Full Simulation In Paparazzi Center
docs.text:
With Paparazzi already installed at ~/paparazzi, run ./kickstart.sh once from the Sensoraia root to link the supplied flight plans, airframes, and unified control panel into ~/paparazzi/conf/:

make native
./kickstart.sh
cd ~/paparazzi && ./paparazzi

In Paparazzi Center, select your camera aircraft (such as Easystar_3_SPOTTERCAM, Easystar_3_AICAM, Easystar_3_LWIRCAM, Easystar_3_CHDKCAM, Easystar_3_EARCAM, Easystar_3_LOOMCAM, Easystar_3_MIMIC, or Bebop_DIPLACAM), pick target nps, and click Build. Then open the Session tab, select the matching Sensoraia \<Camera> NPS session, and click Execute. The session starts USHER for you—do not start local USHER separately. Follow the step-by-step simulation walkthrough.

docs.title: Start Standalone Local USHER
docs.text:
bash examples/paparazzi/run_local_demo.sh --camera spottercam

Leave the terminal open (or edit CAMERA = ... in camera.conf). USHER creates /tmp/usher-sim and prints capture diagnostics. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished; never run it simultaneously with a Center session that already starts USHER.

docs.title: Connect A Simulated Aircraft
docs.text:
Follow Paparazzi integration to install the supplied plans and select a matching NPS session. That guide explains which sessions start USHER for you; use either the session-managed service or the terminal above, never both.

For simulated photographs of real terrain, use MIMIC. It reads your existing aerial tile cache, renders camera views and saves photographs. PANGEA can then map those saved photographs. Missing imagery is reported rather than invented.

Success looks like: a trigger in the simulator, a newly saved JPEG and a completion message in USHER. A GCS photo marker alone means a request was admitted, not necessarily that a file was saved.

docs.title: Try The Real Board On Your Desk
docs.text: Once MORA is prepared and deployed, follow the laptop-to-MORA FTDI desk test. Keep the aircraft simulated while using the real board and cable, first with mock capture and then a physical camera. The illustrated guide includes the dedicated Center session.

docs.title: Prepare The Reference Pi Board
docs.text:
The steps below set up the current Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W reference platform. For another compute board, use its supported Linux image and adapt the OS, service, UART and sensor-runtime steps to that board. The board-independent MORA role does not make Raspberry Pi drivers, GPIO numbers or packages portable automatically.

  1. Install 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Trixie and configure networking and SSH. Follow the board setup guide.
  2. Configure the camera UART on /dev/serial0; disable the serial login console.
  3. Add the service account to the device groups required by your hardware, including dialout for UART and the USB/audio groups used by your setup.
  4. Install runtime packages for your sensor. For stock AIcam this includes the OS camera tools; CHDKbridge needs no extra package, only USB device access for the service account. The sensor guide gives the relevant commands.
  5. Confirm SSH and architecture from the PC:
ssh air@theatre.local 'uname -m; ls -l /dev/serial0; df -h /home/air'

Expect aarch64, an accessible UART device and room for the release and photographs.

docs.title: 1. Cross-Build And Package On The PC
docs.text:
After make all has completed, package the ARM64 applications on the same PC:

make mora-package MORA_INSTALL_DIR=/home/air/sensoraia

The cross-compilers were installed in the PC prerequisite step. The build's private ARM64 SDK already includes ALSA; you do not need to enable system ARM64 multiarch or install libasound2-dev:arm64 for this normal workflow. Packaging refreshes ARM64 binaries as needed and prepares the install package. It does not contact the board or restart a service. Keep the same MORA_INSTALL_DIR for packaging and deployment.

docs.title: 2. Choose Your Camera (camera.conf Or CAMERA=...)
docs.text:
Open camera.conf in the Sensoraia root and set CAMERA to the sensor you want MORA's usher.service to run (spottercam, aicam, lwircam, chdk, earcam, loomcam, or diplacam), or pass CAMERA=<name> directly on the command line without editing any service template:

make mora-package CAMERA=lwircam MORA_INSTALL_DIR=/home/air/sensoraia

The default CAMERA = spottercam starts Spottercam (--spottercam) on the IMX500 AI Camera with nn_vehicles.rpk. All other camera binaries remain installed on MORA so switching cameras later is just changing CAMERA and redeploying. For smaller single-purpose packages, MORA_PROFILE=lwircam or MORA_PROFILE=diplacam remain available. AIcam, Spottercam, and LOOMcam share the same physical IMX500 sensor; run only one of them at a time. See Choose a camera.

docs.title: 3. Upload And Activate
docs.text:
Safe operation is the end user's responsibility.

make mora-deploy \
  MORA_SSH_TARGET=air@theatre.local \
  MORA_INSTALL_DIR=/home/air/sensoraia

Deployment stages the files, checks the package and runtime dependencies, backs up the installed release, and activates the service. The command reports the staging and backup paths.

If activation needs a sudo password, use the interactive procedure in Deployment recovery. Use the staging path printed by your own upload, not one from an old example.

docs.title: 4. Confirm The Installed Release
docs.text:
ssh air@theatre.local 'systemctl --no-pager --full status usher.service'
ssh air@theatre.local 'journalctl -u usher.service -n 50 --no-pager'

Expect the service to be active and the selected sensors to initialize. Make a bench capture, confirm that the JPEG is readable, and inspect its metadata before connecting flight requests. Service startup alone does not confirm capture quality, calibration or sustained operation.

To watch subsequent activity:

ssh -t air@theatre.local 'journalctl -fu usher.service'

Ctrl+C stops log following, not the service.
