  1. Shut MORA down, remove the microSD card, and attach it to the Linux PC. Mount the card's Linux root filesystem partition (typically the larger ext4 partition), not its small FAT boot partition. Set ROOT below to that partition's actual mount point; mount locations vary by PC and desktop.

  2. Generate a WPA2-Personal profile and install it with the permissions NetworkManager requires. Replace the example network name in both places. This command deliberately does not put the password on the command line:

    ROOT=/path/to/mounted/rootfs
nmcli --offline connection add \
   type wifi ifname '*' con-name 'Field WiFi' ssid 'Field WiFi' \
   wifi-sec.key-mgmt wpa-psk connection.autoconnect yes \
   ipv4.method auto ipv6.method auto |
sudo install -D -o root -g root -m 600 /dev/stdin \
   "$ROOT/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/Field-WiFi.nmconnection"

  3. Edit the generated profile as root:

    sudoedit "$ROOT/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/Field-WiFi.nmconnection"

    In its existing [wifi-security] section, add psk=YOUR_WIFI_PASSWORD on a new line. Save the file. Use the actual password, not the placeholder. A WPA2 passphrase is normally 8 to 63 characters; a 64-character hexadecimal key is also accepted. 1. Safely unmount/eject the card from the PC, return it to MORA, and power on the board. Allow time for it to join the access point and obtain an address. Connect using the hostname configured in Imager. If mDNS does not resolve that name, find MORA in the router's DHCP client list and connect using its IP address.

After regaining access, use the previous section to add other Wi-Fi networks.

docs.title: Spottercam: Look For Vehicles
docs.text:
Spottercam turns your airborne camera into a patient lookout. It inspects each captured photograph with a vehicle detector, keeps the original image untouched, and—when combined with aircraft pose and camera geometry—projects spotted vehicles onto the ground and ranks the five best finds as waypoints T1 to T5.

You do not need an airfield or a borrowed firetruck to try it. Start with a single saved picture or the interactive PC flight simulation, where two French 67-CCF firetrucks are parked on the map for your aircraft to discover, and move to MORA and the physical IMX500 AI Camera when you are ready to fly.

Detection terms | AI Camera setup | Paparazzi setup

docs.title: Live Vehicle Search: Detect And Respond
docs.text:
Think of airborne vehicle search as three calm, well-separated jobs:

  1. Capture a clear view along with where the aircraft was and how it was tilted at that moment.
  2. Detect vehicles in the image and record their bounding boxes, subpixel centres and confidence scores in a sidecar file (*.objects.ini) without scribbling over the original photograph.
  3. Project and rank the top five targets (T1..T5) on the ground while leaving the flight plan in complete charge of where the aircraft actually flies.

A bounding box in a photograph is an observation, not a steering command. Even when Spottercam spots a bright red firetruck with high confidence, your flight plan keeps flying its survey rather than diving uninvited toward the truck.

docs.title: Automatic Model Selection
docs.text:
One settings file—modules/spotter_cam/spottercam_settings.ini—serves both real flights on MORA and simulated flights on your PC:

inference_backend=auto
input_source=live
model=models/nn_vehicles.rpk
score_threshold=0.6
class_index=0
max_detections=5
onnx_threads=1
inference_timeout_ms=2000

Why point to .rpk when your laptop does not have an IMX500 sensor wired to its motherboard? Because inference_backend=auto knows the difference:

  • On MORA with the physical IMX500 AI Camera, Spottercam uploads models/nn_vehicles.rpk directly into the camera's onboard neural processor.
  • On a PC in simulation or saved-picture analysis, Spottercam automatically checks modules/spotter_cam/models/ for the matching ONNX exports (vehicle_yolo11n_int8.onnx first, then vehicle_yolo11n_fp32.onnx) with their .ini descriptors and runs whichever ONNX model the CPU runtime supports.

Paths inside the INI are relative to the INI file itself. See choose a model before substituting another export.

Setting Purpose inference_backend=auto Use IMX500 on hardware for .rpk, or probe the sibling CPU .onnx models on PC input_source=live Capture new images from the camera rather than analyse a single fixed file model Select the primary model file; ONNX exports also pair with a same-name .ini descriptor score_threshold, class_index, max_detections Set the minimum confidence (0.6), class (0) and box cap (5) for CPU ONNX detection onnx_threads, inference_timeout_ms Control CPU inference threads and the per-photo timeout in milliseconds

The supplied IMX500 RPK decoder uses class 0 (vehicle), a 0.6 confidence threshold and at most five boxes per image. Model choice and detector settings are ignored when you run in photo-only mode.

PC Demo Assignment What Happens Compatible ONNX export present (direct or sibling of .rpk) Real neural inference on every simulated camera photograph Unset/missing graph without a sibling ONNX export Explicitly labelled seeded random spotting Present but corrupt/incompatible graph or descriptor Clear startup error—never silent random substitution Valid inference with no vehicles in view Zero detections (count=0), recorded cleanly as an empty frame

Random spotting only exists as a fallback when no ONNX model is installed. The normal runtime never invents imaginary vehicles to cover up a broken model.

docs.title: Try A Single Saved Picture First
docs.text:
Want to verify that the detector works on your PC in ten seconds flat, before starting a flight simulator? Run:

make -j32 spottercam
bin/spottercam --check-model --settings modules/spotter_cam/spottercam_settings.ini

To analyse any .jpg photograph on disk (using a fresh copy so no old .objects.ini sidecar is in the way):

cp resources/mock_image_01.jpg /tmp/test-spotter.jpg
rm -f /tmp/test-spotter.objects.ini
bin/spottercam --analyze /tmp/test-spotter.jpg \
  --settings modules/spotter_cam/spottercam_settings.ini --sequence 1
cat /tmp/test-spotter.objects.ini

This runs real CPU ONNX inference without needing a camera attached. Your input JPEG is never re-encoded, and its SHA-256 hash is recorded inside /tmp/test-spotter.objects.ini so detections can never be mixed up with another picture. Build with CAMERA_CAPTURE=0 only on machines where you intentionally skip camera support.

docs.title: Five-Target Mock Survey
docs.text:
In the local simulation, your aircraft flies the survey in examples/paparazzi/conf/flight_plans/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_spotter_cam_demo.xml using the IMX500 camera lens profile (examples/pangea/aicam-2028.ini) and native C USHER (--spottercam --spottercam-targets). On each wings-level shot, USHER captures a mock vehicle scene (resources/mock_aicam_01.jpg), runs the native YOLO11n ONNX detector in bin/spottercam, projects detected vehicles onto the ground from the aircraft's pose, and sends ranked target updates for waypoints T1..T5 directly over the simulated UART (digital_cam_point).

Follow these steps to fly the mission manually from takeoff to landing in Paparazzi Center—no physical camera, MORA board, or Python helper is needed:

docs.title: 1. Build Native PC Binaries And Install Paparazzi Links
docs.text:
From the Sensoraia root (with Paparazzi installed in ~/paparazzi):

make usher soda spottercam
./kickstart.sh

docs.title: 2. Launch Paparazzi Center, Build NPS, And Execute The Session
docs.text:
Start Paparazzi Center from your Paparazzi directory:

cd ~/paparazzi
MORA_UART_DEVICE="" ./paparazzi

(Setting MORA_UART_DEVICE="" forces PC-only simulation even if an FTDI cable is plugged in.)

In Paparazzi Center:

  1. Set Config to userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_conf.xml and Control panel to userconf/SENSORAIA/sensoraia_demo_control_panel.xml (./kickstart.sh selects both by default).
  2. Select aircraft Easystar_3_SPOTTERCAM and target nps, then click Build.
  3. Open the Session tab, choose Sensoraia Spottercam NPS, and click Execute (starting Sensoraia USHER, Sensoraia NPS, Data Link, Server, and GCS Classic).

docs.title: 3. Take Off, Watch T1–T5 Update, And Land
docs.text:
In GCS Classic:

  1. Wait a few seconds until the aircraft icon appears and GPS shows a valid 3D fix (Wait GPS switches to Holding point).
  2. Click Takeoff in the GCS strip.
  3. The aircraft climbs, spirals down at SOUTHWEST to the $44\text{ m}$ AGL survey height, and enters Survey (you can also click Find vehicle at any time from Standby).
  4. Every three seconds on wings-level survey legs (bank angle within 12°), the autopilot triggers a shot. USHER runs native YOLO11n ONNX detection in bin/spottercam, ranks confidence (0..1000) across the five target slots (once all five slots are full, a strictly higher score replaces the lowest one), and transmits correlated USHER_CAM_POINT_UPDATE messages over the simulated UART so the flight plan moves T1..T5 onto the projected coordinates using the ordinary GCS waypoint-update mechanism (WP_MOVED).
  5. After the 160-second survey completes, the aircraft automatically flies its baseleg, final glide, and flare to touchdown. Stop all session programs in Center when finished.

docs.title: 4. Inspect Your Saved Photos And Detections
docs.text:
Check ~/Pictures/sensoraia/ after the flight:

Saved File Or Folder What You Will Find Inside ~/Pictures/sensoraia/ma*.jpg Saved mock camera JPEGs tagged with EXIF flight pose and Spottercam detection summary ~/Pictures/sensoraia/ma*.objects.ini Validated USHER_OBJECTS_V2 sidecars with bounding boxes, centres, scores, and SHA-256 bindings ~/Pictures/sensoraia/detections/ Convenience copies of photographs containing accepted vehicle detections

Locating real image boxes requires pose and camera projection. The supplied projection profile is illustrative, not a measured calibration. Unusable geometry (such as a steep bank during a U-turn) does not authorize moving a waypoint, and a valid model can find fewer than five objects or none.

docs.title: Use A Physical Camera
docs.text: When you move from your desk to the airfield with a real vehicle on the ground, Spottercam runs on MORA with the Raspberry Pi AI Camera (IMX500) and executes modules/spotter_cam/models/nn_vehicles.rpk directly on the camera's neural chip.

docs.title: 1. Check The Camera And Model Selection On Your PC
docs.text:
Spottercam is already the default camera (CAMERA = spottercam in camera.conf), which configures MORA's usher.service with:

ExecStart=/home/air/sensoraia/usher --spottercam

And modules/spotter_cam/spottercam_settings.ini already selects model=models/nn_vehicles.rpk with inference_backend=auto.

Whenever you want MORA to boot with a different sensor instead of Spottercam, edit CAMERA in camera.conf (or pass CAMERA=<name> to make mora-deploy—no service-file editing required):

Desired MORA Startup Mode camera.conf / make mora-deploy Setting Spottercam (default: IMX500 + nn_vehicles.rpk) CAMERA=spottercam AIcam (IMX500 native photos, no model) CAMERA=aicam LWIRcam (Tiny1-C / TDK USB thermal camera) CAMERA=lwircam CHDKbridge (Canon USB camera with CHDK) CAMERA=chdk EARcam (USB microphone acoustic search) CAMERA=earcam LOOMcam (visual homing framework on IMX500) CAMERA=loomcam Diplacam (native GP/diffusion field planner) CAMERA=diplacam

Spottercam, AIcam and LOOMcam are alternative owners of the same physical IMX500 ribbon camera—pick one at a time. To package a custom Spottercam settings file and its model, pass MORA_SPOTTERCAM_SETTINGS=/absolute/path/spottercam_settings.ini to make mora-deploy. See deploy and select a profile and model selection.

docs.title: 2. Build And Deploy To MORA
docs.text:
Prepare the AI Camera hardware (connect the ribbon cable with power off). Then, from the Sensoraia root on your PC, build and deploy the release to MORA:

make all
make mora-deploy MORA_SSH_TARGET=air@theatre.local MORA_INSTALL_DIR=/home/air/sensoraia

Confirm that usher.service is active and running --spottercam:

ssh air@theatre.local 'systemctl --no-pager --full status usher.service'
ssh air@theatre.local 'journalctl -u usher.service -n 50 --no-pager'

docs.title: 3. Perform A Bench Or Flight-Line Check Before Takeoff
docs.text:
Before launching the aircraft, verify that the IMX500 camera and nn_vehicles.rpk capture and analyse a real frame cleanly (discovering a lens cap on the bench is much nicer than discovering it at $44\text{ m}$).

Either trigger a single camera-2 shot from your connected flight controller (or FTDI desk setup), or run a standalone check on MORA by stopping the service briefly, taking one test photo, and starting the service again:

bin/spottercam --probe /home/air/sensoraia/models/ai_cam/nn_vehicles.rpk
bin/spottercam --capture /home/air/sensoraia/models/ai_cam/nn_vehicles.rpk /home/air/Pictures/bench-check.jpg

Initial RPK upload to the IMX500 takes a few seconds longer than subsequent shots. Always use a new output filename and restart usher.service after a standalone test so USHER owns the camera for flight.

docs.title: 4. Fly The Real Survey And Inspect Captured Evidence
docs.text:
1. Flash or configure your autopilot with digital_cam_uart and the survey flight plan (sensoraia_spotter_cam_demo.xml, adjusted for your airfield's coordinates and safe altitude).
  2. Connect the flight-controller UART to MORA (/dev/serial0, 115200 baud, 3.3 V logic, crossed TX/RX and common ground) and power the system.
  3. After takeoff, enter Find vehicle (Start demo $\rightarrow$ Survey). On each periodic trigger, USHER captures a $2028 \times 1520$ JPEG and on-sensor nn_vehicles.rpk detections, writes synchronized flight EXIF (SENSOR02 frame timing, GPS, attitude, and detection summary), and copies any photograph with a vehicle hit into ~/Pictures/sensoraia/detections/ while SODA writes annotated review crops.
  4. After landing, retrieve the original a*.jpg photos, a*.objects.ini sidecars, and detections/ copies from /home/air/Pictures/sensoraia/.

docs.title: Optional: Native Photo-Only Mode On MORA
docs.text:
If you want fast native IMX500 photographs without loading a model or running detection, simply deploy with CAMERA=aicam (make mora-deploy CAMERA=aicam), or run --spottercam --native-photo in a standalone session.

Repackage and deploy after changing the line. --native-photo needs no model, cannot be combined with --spottercam-settings, and saves a $2028 \times 1520$ quality-90 JPEG with sensor timing evidence but no detection metadata or SODA analysis. For a standalone photo-only check on MORA from /home/air/sensoraia (with usher.service stopped):

bin/spottercam --photo-only --probe
bin/spottercam --photo-only --capture /home/air/Pictures/spotter-photo.jpg

Restore usher.service afterward. See native photographs and the camera speed test for timing and throughput options.

docs.title: Use LWIR Photos (Future & Multi-Sensor Option)
docs.text:
LWIRcam can remain the sole Tiny1C camera owner while a separate persistent Spottercam CPU worker analyses each completed thermal JPEG. Its assignment is independent of the AI Camera assignment. Supply an ONNX detector trained and independently evaluated on representative Tiny1C imagery, plus its matching spotter_boxes_xyxy_v1 descriptor. The supplied modules/spotter_cam/spottercam_lwir_settings.ini is a template, not a trained thermal model. Keep the inference image rendering consistent with training. This includes JPEG quality, which normal LWIR captures now default to 95. Legends are rejected and missing real temperature/frame evidence is an error.

make usher spottercam CAMERA_CAPTURE=0
bin/spottercam --check-model --settings /absolute/lwir-detector.ini
./usher --lwircam --lwir-spotter-settings /absolute/lwir-detector.ini

Capture and flight EXIF complete before inference enters the existing bounded saved-file queue. One warm detector retains the model; source images and temperature planes are never rewritten. Overflow retains originals for offline analysis. Detector errors never discard a photo or reuse an earlier detection. SODA retries do not repeat object inference. This is asynchronous per-photo analysis, not a promise to analyse every camera stream frame.

Each accepted result has an .objects.ini model record and an additional .lwir-objects.ini record binding the photo number, frame/boot identity, source and model hashes, native subpixel centres and nearest-pixel temperatures. Invalid endpoint temperature codes are reported unavailable, not converted to Celsius. A valid zero-detection result is different from failed analysis. Results are local evidence; this option does not move aircraft waypoints or add new flight-controller messages. Existing SODA AI-camera EXIF summaries are not automatically written into these unchanged LWIR originals.

To enable geographic estimates, additionally supply a measured native 256x192 PANGEA_CAMERA_V1 profile with the l prefix, correct intrinsics and mounting:

./usher --lwircam --lwir-spotter-settings /absolute/lwir-detector.ini \
  --lwir-spotter-profile /absolute/measured-lwir-camera.ini \
  --lwir-spotter-limits 5000,1

The limits are maximum exposure-interval width in microseconds and maximum pose uncertainty in metres. Defaults are 5000 us and 1 m, not measured accuracy. Projection requires an exposure-qualified aligned pose belonging to the exact frame. Frame arrival alone, missing pose/calibration, broad timing or excessive uncertainty leaves detections and temperatures usable but omits target latitude and longitude. Use the existing clock alignment and measured --lwir-latency-ms MIN,MAX facilities where applicable; never guess latency or relax limits merely to obtain coordinates. All three aircraft attitude axes and camera mounting rotations are applied through shared geometry. Detector centres retain subpixel precision; only temperature sampling rounds to a native pixel. Ground projection assumes a local flat surface and a calibrated pinhole camera. Lens distortion, terrain, target elevation and physical timing/calibration errors still require independent field validation; extra decimal places do not prove pinpoint accuracy. Temperatures remain device-reported and uncalibrated.

An opt-in package includes the detector and chosen model without changing the ordinary LWIR-only default:

make mora-package MORA_PROFILE=lwircam \
  MORA_LWIR_SPOTTER_SETTINGS=/absolute/lwir-detector.ini

The package enables saved-photo detection but does not invent a projection calibration. Deploy separately only when the selected trained model is ready. Measure latency and total shared 512 MB board headroom with the real model.

docs.title: Keep The Evidence
docs.text:
USHER stores the selected detection summary with the original JPEG's flight metadata. SODA may make annotated/cropped review copies and a detection log. The original flight photo remains undecorated.

A bounding box is an image result, not automatically a geographic target. Where a valid target is integrated, the flight plan still decides whether to visit it. Confidence, target freshness and geographic accuracy are different questions.

docs.title: Supply A Different Vehicle Model
docs.text:
An arbitrary YOLO export or unrelated RPK is not automatically compatible. Keep the class mapping, preprocessing and output contract with the export. If using a Vehicles dataset, retain its exact source/version, permitted use and independent evaluation. The filename does not identify the dataset release or establish detector accuracy.

MIMIC views or saved photos may support external evaluation where imagery rights permit. Choose views representative of the camera, add independent labels and separate evaluation data. A north-up map or annotated SODA crop is not automatically a ready-made training dataset.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom What To Check First local mode is already running or /tmp/usher-sim busy Stop the previous Center session or remove /tmp/usher-sim after confirming no USHER is running Want hardware-in-the-loop over FTDI instead of PC USHER Select the Sensoraia MORA desk NPS session in Paparazzi Center (see the desk-test guide) --mock-map needs zoom-18 XYZ JPEGs Pan over the survey area at zoom 18 in PprzGCS so ~/.local/share/paparazzi/pprzgcs/map/GOOGLE/18 is populated Photos saved (ma*.jpg), but T1..T5 stay at HOME Check the USHER console and *.objects.ini sidecars; shots during steep turns (bank angle 12° or more) are skipped by the flight plan Real MORA camera busy Ensure only one IMX500 owner (--spottercam, --aicam, or --loomcam) is running; stop usher.service before standalone --probe or --capture

Model errors stop fresh target publication; existing points are not proof of new observations. Check the selected assignment and worker log before restarting. A successful image with zero detections is not an analysis failure. For hardware problems, check camera ownership, cabling and runtime packages. Validate camera geometry, timing and loaded MORA resources separately before relying on real-flight locations.

docs.title: Capture With USHER
docs.text:
USHER connects an aircraft's capture requests to the selected sensors on MORA. It saves the observation, keeps the available flight information with it, and reports the outcome. You can try the same flow on a Linux PC before connecting hardware.

Install and get started | Glossary | Simulated flights

docs.title: Compute-Board Baseline
docs.text: MORA is the onboard-computer role, not a Raspberry Pi model. Sensoraia starts from the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W as a deliberately constrained 512 MB ARM64 reference. The current ready-made cross-build and deployment workflow targets 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Trixie and Cortex-A53. A different compute board can host Sensoraia when its OS/ABI, drivers, peripherals and resource budget are compatible; it may need a board-specific build profile, package and service configuration. The Pi baseline is not proof that every module fits or runs unchanged on every board.

docs.title: Choose A Camera
docs.text:
You never need to edit systemd unit templates by hand to switch sensors. Pick your camera in whichever way matches how you are running Sensoraia:

  1. For MORA deployment & local standalone runs: Set CAMERA = <name> in camera.conf at the repository root, or pass CAMERA=<name> on the command line (make mora-deploy CAMERA=lwircam, or bash examples/paparazzi/run_local_demo.sh --camera lwircam).
  2. For Paparazzi Center simulation: Select the matching aircraft and session in the GUI after running ./kickstart.sh.
CAMERA value USHER CLI Flag Paparazzi Center Aircraft & Session Use It For Start Here spottercam (default) --spottercam Easystar_3_SPOTTERCAM / Sensoraia Spottercam NPS Visible IMX500 photos + vehicle detection (T1..T5) Spottercam aicam --aicam --native-photo (or --aicam) Easystar_3_AICAM / Sensoraia AIcam NPS Plain Raspberry Pi AI Camera photographs AI Camera lwircam --lwircam Easystar_3_LWIRCAM / Sensoraia LWIRcam NPS Tiny1-C / TDK USB thermal capture LWIRcam chdk --chdk Easystar_3_CHDKCAM / Sensoraia CHDKcam NPS Canon compact camera running CHDK over USB PTP CHDKbridge earcam --earcam Easystar_3_EARCAM / Sensoraia EARcam NPS Microphone observations and acoustic search EARcam loomcam --loomcam Easystar_3_LOOMCAM / Sensoraia LOOMcam NPS Experimental visual-return observations LOOMcam diplacam --diplacam-config FILE Bebop_DIPLACAM / Sensoraia Diplacam NPS Experimental 8-waypoint rotorcraft planner Diplacam

AIcam, Spottercam and LOOMcam are alternative owners of the same physical IMX500 camera; do not start them together. A USB microphone and a supported thermal camera are separate devices, but their combined resource use still needs checking on MORA. MORA_PROFILE=lwircam and MORA_PROFILE=diplacam remain available when you want a smaller single-sensor MORA package instead of the full-suite package. Selecting a backend does not install board OS camera packages or physical calibration files.

docs.title: Building And Deploying USHER
docs.text:
Follow Build on your PC for local binaries and Deploy to MORA for cross-building, packaging and activation. The root make help lists the supported commands.

After installing the PC prerequisites, make all prepares its missing SDKs and source dependencies, builds every PC and ARM64 application, and checks the complete executable list. The same command works after make clean; no private camera-library checkout or manual SDK recovery is required.

Building and packaging do not contact MORA. Activation is a separate step that restarts USHER. Keep model/settings changes with the release you deploy.

docs.title: Start Here: Local Simulation
docs.text:
For a full simulated flight, use the Paparazzi demo walkthrough. Its Center sessions start the sensor companion, simulator and ground tools together. Do not start another USHER beside a session that already owns it.

For a terminal-only camera peer, use:

bash examples/paparazzi/run_local_demo.sh

This starts local mock capture, not a complete flight. Leave the terminal open while your simulated aircraft connects. Stop it with Ctrl+C afterwards. MIMIC supplies views of cached terrain when you want changing camera imagery instead of a fixed test picture.

docs.title: Deploy To MORA
docs.text: Complete the installation and activation steps, then check the selected sensors on the bench. A running service means the program started; it does not establish that a camera is focused, a microphone gain is suitable or a geographic estimate is accurate.

docs.title: When Sudo Requires Your Password
docs.text:
For completely hands-free make mora-deploy runs with zero password prompts, you can configure passwordless sudo on MORA or create /home/air/pass.txt (chmod 600 /home/air/pass.txt, replacing replacewithyourpass with your MORA sudo password) as shown in the desk-test automation guide.

If you prefer interactive sudo and upload succeeded before activation reported that sudo needs a password, connect with ssh air@theatre.local. In that same MORA terminal, substitute the exact staging path printed by your upload:

stage=/home/air/sensoraia/.deploy.XXXXXXXX
[[ -s "$stage/deploy_mora_remote.sh" ]] && sudo -v && \
   bash "$stage/deploy_mora_remote.sh" /home/air/sensoraia "$stage"

Use your installation directory/account. sudo -v authenticates subsequent privileged operations in this terminal; another SSH session may not share it. This resumes the uploaded release's normal activation path, so no new build/upload is needed merely to enter a password.

If activation fails, inspect the reported error and service journal before trying again. Keep the previous release and the deployment's backup until you have confirmed the new one works.

docs.title: Start Here: Physical Desk Test With MORA
docs.text:
For a laptop running NPS connected by FTDI, use the illustrated desk-test guide. It explains the cable's 5 V power output, crossed 3.3 V UART, Center session and mock-to-real sequence.

Connect the FC-to-MORA UART with the documented voltage levels and a common ground. Camera and microphone connections go to MORA, not to that UART.

  1. Check the selected sensor by following its standalone capture/listening guide. Stop any existing owner before opening the same device separately.
  2. Restore or start the reviewed USHER service configuration.
  3. Send one capture request through the connected flight controller.
  4. Check the saved file and the completion result, not just a GCS photo dot.
  5. Inspect focus, expected image dimensions and the available flight metadata.

For service status and recent diagnostics:

systemctl --no-pager --full status usher.service
journalctl -u usher.service -n 50 --no-pager

Run these on MORA, either in an SSH session or a local terminal. Take one sensor at a time through this check before combining workloads.

docs.title: Find Your Results
docs.text:
USHER's usual photo directory is ~/Pictures/sensoraia/ for the account running it. The service account and any explicit output settings determine the actual location. A simulation companion prints its own session directory.

Keep original JPEGs. SODA can make separate annotated/cropped review images; PANGEA can make maps from accepted originals. Neither is a reason to replace the original capture with an edited copy.

What You See What It Means A GCS shot marker A trigger was admitted; inspect completion to confirm a saved image A saved, readable JPEG Image capture completed; optional analysis may still fail Zero accepted detections A successful model run may have found no accepted objects An invalid or missing point Do not treat it as a new geographic target A map or sound picture A derived result; retain its source observations too

docs.title: Position And Timing
docs.text:
For measured still-image throughput on MORA or a PC, follow the Camera Speed Test. Sensor frame rate and saved-image throughput are different measurements.

The aircraft keeps moving between a request and the actual measurement. Sensoraia records available pose and timing evidence, but not every camera provides the same exposure information. A request-time geotag must not be mistaken for a demonstrated exposure-time position.

See image metadata for what to inspect and the glossary for pose, latency and uncertainty. Use measured camera geometry and mounting when turning image positions into ground locations.

docs.title: Hotspot GPS Coordinates And Center Temperatures
docs.text: Thermal geolocation needs a supported temperature plane, enabled analysis, camera calibration, mounting information and a suitable observation pose. Follow the thermal calibration guide before relying on projected locations. Image-only thermal capture cannot supply missing temperature measurements.

docs.title: LWIR Integration And Effective Lag
docs.text: Capture delay, pose timing and camera mounting are separate sources of error. A sharper display or a timing label alone does not validate them. Use the thermal guide's independent target checks, and inspect the recorded timing information rather than assuming the request and exposure coincide.

docs.title: Spottercam
docs.text: Use the Spottercam guide for model selection and same-image detections. A box in image coordinates needs valid projection and a flight-plan integration before it becomes a geographic target.

docs.title: EARcam Acoustic Backend
docs.text: EARcam combines sound measurements with aircraft positions. Keep microphone gain fixed during a search, and inspect whether the result is usable rather than assuming every completed search returns a reliable location. Follow the sound-search guide.

docs.title: If Something Stops
docs.text:
Symptom Check First Local endpoint already in use Stop the previous simulator/sensor session; do not start a second owner Camera busy or unavailable Check cabling, device permissions and other camera clients No saved photograph Read the capture error and check free space/output permissions Model rejected Check that the graph, descriptor and settings belong together Photo saved but no review copy There may be zero detections or an analysis error; inspect the original's metadata and worker log Target updates stop Inspect freshness/model/confirmation diagnostics; the existing target is not a fresh observation

For the available options, run ./usher --help and the selected sensor's --help. Diagnose the stage that failed before repeating a physical capture.

docs.title: Tailor Or Add A Module
docs.text:
Each Sensoraia sensor module is self-contained under modules/<module>/:

  1. Tailor an existing module: Edit its C/C++ sources or settings file under modules/<module>/ (for example modules/lwir_cam/ or modules/ear_cam/), update its modules/<module>/README.md and modules/<module>/docs/*.md guide, and run make all to rebuild both PC and ARM64 binaries cleanly.
  2. Create a new module: - Create modules/<your_module>/ with your C11/C++17 worker source, README.md, and docs/<your-module>.md user guide (keeping within MORA's 512 MB total shared RAM and avoiding Python on MORA). - Register the backend in src/camera_backend_registry.c using the shared struct camera_backend interface in src/camera_backend.h while keeping src/usher_protocol.h wire-compatible with the flight controller. - Add your build rule to build-support/make/camera-modules.mk (and SUITE_APPLICATIONS in Makefile plus build-support/mora-package.list if packaged for MORA) and expose a CAMERA option in camera.conf and build-support/package_mora.sh.
  3. Share via Fork & Pull Request: Fork sensoraia on GitHub, commit your module and documentation updates on a feature branch, verify make all, and open a Pull Request.
